stops.name: Gola di Gorropu
stops.detail: The Gorropu Gorge is a deep canyon located in Supramonte, Sardinia, and demarcates the border between the municipalities of Orgosolo and Urzulei. In the variety of the local language, gorropu indicates a cliff or excavated area. The throat originated as a result of the opening of a fault and thanks to the intense erosive action caused by the waters of the Rio Flumineddu. The Gorropu Gorge, with its walls up to over 500 m high and a width that varies from 4 meters to the closest points to reach some tens in others, is considered the deepest canyon in Italy and one of the deepest in Europe. Its walls contain fossils that reveal the underwater genesis, which occurred between 190 and 60 million years ago.
